W.note: Grip's slow start and Stop's fast launch are clearly different, Catch adds a visible kick, the shared 1.6 s clock with hold and rest reads cleanly, and the graph playhead, values, reduced-motion start and pause all work.

X.note: Snap, Stick and Thud are distinct on paper, but the page is bare track-and-ball with only a spec line, no pause control, no curve graph, and no reduced-motion handling.

Y.note: The graph with a time playhead, computed peak and settle readouts, and the ease-out reference make the curves very legible, though Press and Catch overlap in shape and the CSS pause rule blocks Play under reduced motion.

Z.note: Values are copyable and the names say sticky or punchy, but there is no graph, no pause, no reduced-motion handling, and Sticky Snap is a generic ease-in-out that overlaps the others, while Sticky Punch's undershoot pushes the ball past the track edge.
